newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT MKT OUTLOOK--Jobless claims, tight range.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT MKT OUTLOOK--Jobless claims, tight range.

text.p: U.S. credit market players will read the nation's weekly jobless claims sheet on Thursday, but Treasury instruments are expected to remain in a narrow band, analysts said.

The market receives claims at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. Yet, market pundits asserted Treasuries have little to guide them other than some consolidation from the positive technicals and sentiment that supported them early in the week.
"(Thursday) really has nothing at all to move the market...just more consolidation," said John Park, an economist at Sanwa Securities (USA) Co.
Treasury prices rallied sharply on Tuesday, following Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's market-friendly Humphrey- Hawkins House testimony.
Treasuries at times had difficulty on Wednesday, especially when the September contract tried to break above 115-16/32, which it eventually did.
Based on late trade Wednesday, however, Park said the market does not seem to have any impetus in either direction.
Some experts said they saw room for upward price activity in the belly of the yield curve.

"The two- and five-years are still relatively cheap to where we were -- as far as the yield curve goes -- at the highs in the market," said a senior trader, referring to the yield spreads back in January 1996.
He said the jobless claims report is likely to induce more "day-trading reactionary type of responses" as opposed to a "fundamental shift" due to a fundamental perception change in the market.
For instance, a higher level of continuing claims would indicate that the unemployment rate may not move higher for the month of July, added Kretzmer.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast, on average, that new claims for state unemployment insurance fell to 333,000 in the week ended July 19 versus 349,000 in the prior week.
Peter Kretzmer, senior economist at Nationsbanc Capital Markets Inc, said he expected new claims to fall back from last week's level.

"Most of the decline reflects people's judgment that most of the (recent) rise was related to the auto plant closings," he said. Kretzmer said he would watch continuing claims as a guide to his forecast for the upcoming unemployment rate, slated for Friday next week.
